# quotient ring　`def.quotient-ring`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.quotient-ring)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.quotient-ring.md)

**Universal property**: if $f : A \to B$ is a ring homomorphism with $f(I) = 0$, then there is a unique ring homomorphism $\bar f : A/I \to B$ with $\bar f \circ \pi = f$.

## Notes · **stale**
⭐ Why an ideal is necessary: for $(a+x)(b+y) \equiv ab \pmod I$ one needs $ay, xb, xy \in I$; since $x, y \in I$ while $a, b$ are arbitrary, $I$ must absorb multiplication from both sides.

⭐ Examples: $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$; $K[x]/(f)$ (a field when $f$ is irreducible); $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{2}+1)$.
